newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Coal, banks loom large in Colombia privatizations.
newsitem.headline: Coal, banks loom large in Colombia privatizations.

text.p: The sale of coal mining company Carbones de Colombia and savings bank Concasa will take center stage in the government's on-going privatization plan in 1997, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Thursday.
The government, he said, hoped to be able to offer packets of shares in the company to the general public rather than just to large institutional bidders as has so far been the case.
Carbones de Colombia (Carbocol) has a 50 percent stake in the giant Cerrejon Zona Norte mine in northern Guajira province, which it operates in conjunction with a Colombian unit of the Exxon Corp.
Ocampo said he hoped the sale of Carbocol would net the government about $500 million. The central bank recently forecast Carbocol could fetch as much as $600 million.
The sale of its 61 percent in savings bank and building society Concasa could bring the government about $110 million, Ocampo said.

The timetable for privatization for 1997 will also include the sell-off of minority stakes in Banco Popular, now controlled by finance magnate Luis Carlos Sarmiento, in the Banco Colombiano de Comercio Exterior and further sales in the energy sector.
